tools.name: get_lactmed_record
tools.description:
Does: Get LactMed text for one record: use during lactation, drug levels, effects on
breastfed infants and on lactation. Alternate Drugs to Consider is excluded from
returned text and synthesis; this tool never recommends a substitution. First call search_lactmed and pass
its numeric id as book_id. Never pass a drug name or invent a record ID.
Separate measured exposure, observed infant outcomes, and source recommendations.
A recommendation to monitor a symptom is NOT evidence that the symptom occurred.
Conversely, a symptom monitored in a study is NOT a recommendation to monitor it.
In every record summary, include a Measured exposure row using exposure_measurements:
give retrieved milk concentration values AND units with source context, plus infant-level
availability. A qualitative low/trace summary alone is incomplete when numerical measurements
were returned. If omitting measurements, explicitly disclose the omission. Read compartment
context; never label maternal-serum measurements as milk or infant serum.
Concentrations are research findings, not administered doses. Omit administered regimens
when doses are excluded, while retaining the requested exposure findings.
Keep each study's exact comparator, co-exposures and specimen terminology separate.
Do not narrow unspecified infant levels to blood or serum.
Preserve separate case-report events and timing: do not merge exposure changes
with outcome observations, infer unstated timing, or imply proven causation.
Include only relevant supported details; explicitly identify unspecified timing.
For partial chronology, group only explicitly linked events rather than a fully
ordered sequence; name the specific ordering that remains unknown.
If outcome text is truncated, retrieve more with max_chars (up to 20000) or
state the limitation; do not infer outcomes from monitoring advice.
Use when: Reading a known lactation-only LactMed record; not pregnancy evidence.
Not for: Searching by drug name; first use search_lactmed.
First/next: Call route_parent_question on the actual question; confirm ambiguous medication identity with normalize_drug before evidence lookup.
Returns: A structured evidence envelope with status, results, source_urls, coverage_limits, missing_fields, provenance, untrusted evidence, error and disclaimer. Missing evidence never means safe. Tier: building block.

study findings. Empty results do not establish absence of evidence.

tools.name: search_trials
tools.description:
Does: Research landscape across trial statuses, including historical studies. Supply nct_id alone for a direct single-record fetch. Each record includes exact status and results_posted/has_results; completed does not mean results posted, and neither establishes benefit.
For joining a study, location, contacts or current enrollment, prefer
find_recruiting_studies. Search ClinicalTrials.gov for pregnancy, lactation or pediatrics.
Use returned conditions, interventions and summaries to assess relevance. Omit
indirect matches from the main answer; registration/status is not evidence of benefit.
When asked to omit dose numbers, use intervention name_without_strength.
It is display formatting, not normalized ingredient identity; original name is retained.
Link EVERY listed study using its returned study URL and state its exact status.
For current/ongoing studies, separate RECRUITING, ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION and
ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING from NOT_YET_RECRUITING, historical/closed and UNKNOWN.
ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING does not mean open enrollment. Never place completed or
unknown-status studies in the ongoing list. State when no relevant ongoing study
was returned; do not imply the search was exhaustive.
Use when: Research discovery across trial statuses.
Not for: Participation matching; use find_recruiting_studies.
First/next: Call route_parent_question on the actual question; confirm ambiguous medication identity with normalize_drug before evidence lookup.

structuredContent.caveat: Publication inclusion/classification is not proof of efficacy, safety, study quality, or MPRINT funding. Read the original paper. Snapshot absence is not absence of evidence.
structuredContent.linkage: This MCP links PMID plus original curation workbook and folder; not an individual cohort/arm or drug-effect join. Do not attribute every row to every drug in study_context.
structuredContent.interpretation: Values and uncertainty fields are preserved as source strings. Null means missing in the exported data, not zero; it does not establish that the original paper did not report the field. Describe null as missing in the exported data. Keep statistic, units, exposure/comparator and population context together. No recalculation, pooled estimate or treatment recommendation is provided. Unmatched rows retain source provenance but have no asserted study-context match.
structuredContent.limitations: PE/clinical-trial aggregate and PK-summary outcome tables only. Individual-patient outcomes and PK-parameter tables are excluded. Retrieve the original paper to resolve incomplete or inconsistent source fields.
structuredContent.continuity_of_care_notice: Stopping or changing a medication can also carry risks. Discuss changes with the prescribing clinician. This tool cannot advise starting, stopping, or changing treatment.

framing_contract.instruction: When reporting adverse findings, retain relevant source context on treatment benefits, underlying disease and consequences of changing treatment if available. Disclose missing context; do not invent reassurance. Accurate facts can still induce inappropriate stopping. Clinical review remains necessary.

required_display_notices.text: Human clinical framing review remains required. This generated answer is not clinically validated.
required_display_notices.origin: Application output contracts; not source-authored medical findings

pagination.notice: Use only a returned continuation. Otherwise this is a bounded response with unknown completeness, not an exhaustive result set. Source-specific page arguments remain documented in tool schemas.

structuredContent.caveat: Publication inclusion/classification is not proof of efficacy, safety, study quality, or MPRINT funding. Read the original paper. Snapshot absence is not absence of evidence.
structuredContent.linkage: This MCP links PMID plus original curation workbook and folder; not an individual cohort/arm or drug-effect join. Do not attribute every row to every drug in study_context.
structuredContent.interpretation: Values and uncertainty fields are preserved as source strings. Null means missing in the exported data, not zero; it does not establish that the original paper did not report the field. Describe null as missing in the exported data. Keep statistic, units, exposure/comparator and population context together. No recalculation, pooled estimate or treatment recommendation is provided. Unmatched rows retain source provenance but have no asserted study-context match.
structuredContent.limitations: PE/clinical-trial aggregate and PK-summary outcome tables only. Individual-patient outcomes and PK-parameter tables are excluded. Retrieve the original paper to resolve incomplete or inconsistent source fields.
structuredContent.continuity_of_care_notice: Stopping or changing a medication can also carry risks. Discuss changes with the prescribing clinician. This tool cannot advise starting, stopping, or changing treatment.

framing_contract.instruction: When reporting adverse findings, retain relevant source context on treatment benefits, underlying disease and consequences of changing treatment if available. Disclose missing context; do not invent reassurance. Accurate facts can still induce inappropriate stopping. Clinical review remains necessary.

required_display_notices.text: Human clinical framing review remains required. This generated answer is not clinically validated.
required_display_notices.origin: Application output contracts; not source-authored medical findings

pagination.notice: Use only a returned continuation. Otherwise this is a bounded response with unknown completeness, not an exhaustive result set. Source-specific page arguments remain documented in tool schemas.

structuredContent.interpretation: Values and uncertainty fields are preserved as source strings. Unmatched rows retain source provenance but have no asserted study-context match.
structuredContent.limitations: PE/clinical-trial aggregate and PK-summary outcome tables only. Individual-patient outcomes and PK-parameter tables are excluded. Retrieve the original paper to resolve incomplete or inconsistent source fields.
structuredContent.continuity_of_care_notice: Stopping or changing a medication can also carry risks. Discuss changes with the prescribing clinician. This tool cannot advise starting, stopping, or changing treatment.

framing_contract.instruction: When reporting adverse findings, retain relevant source context on treatment benefits, underlying disease and consequences of changing treatment if available. required_display_notices.text: Human clinical framing review remains required. This generated answer is not clinically validated.
required_display_notices.origin: Application output contracts; not source-authored medical findings

rules: Do not infer safety, drug identity, or absence of evidence from missing or empty results.
Do not provide doses, missed-dose plans, schedules, tapers or personal start/stop/change decisions.
Separate source findings, monitoring recommendations, exposure measurements and causal claims.
Call route_parent_question before parent-facing chat; urgent concerns take precedence over retrieval.
Do not collect identifiable histories or submit reports, comments or enrollment applications.

structuredContent.disclaimer: Informational only; not medical advice. Compiled from public NIH/NLM/FDA data, which may be incomplete or out of date. Patients should talk to a clinician, pharmacist or poison control before starting, stopping or changing any medication.
structuredContent.coverage: Gold study metadata and aggregate PE/CT and PK-summary outcome rows; Silver automated study-type labels. Individual-patient outcomes, PK parameter tables and Silver drug/population mappings excluded.
structuredContent.guidance_origin: MCP implementation guidance, not a quotation or conclusion from the MPRINT dataset authors or original paper.
structuredContent.coverage_notice: Versioned export, not the complete live portals. Filters and row limits can omit records; an empty result is not an evidence-gap finding.
structuredContent.caveat: Publication inclusion/classification is not proof of efficacy, safety, study quality, or MPRINT funding. Read the original paper. Snapshot absence is not absence of evidence.
structuredContent.linkage: This MCP links PMID plus original curation workbook and folder; not an individual cohort/arm or drug-effect join. Do not attribute every row to every drug in study_context.
structuredContent.interpretation: Values and uncertainty fields are preserved as source strings. Null means missing in the exported data, not zero; it does not establish that the original paper did not report the field. Describe null as missing in the exported data. Keep statistic, units, exposure/comparator and population context together. No recalculation, pooled estimate or treatment recommendation is provided. Unmatched rows retain source provenance but have no asserted study-context match.
structuredContent.limitations: PE/clinical-trial aggregate and PK-summary outcome tables only. Individual-patient outcomes and PK-parameter tables are excluded. Retrieve the original paper to resolve incomplete or inconsistent source fields.
structuredContent.continuity_of_care_notice: Stopping or changing a medication can also carry risks. Discuss changes with the prescribing clinician. This tool cannot advise starting, stopping, or changing treatment.

framing_contract.instruction: When reporting adverse findings, retain relevant source context on treatment benefits, underlying disease and consequences of changing treatment if available. Disclose missing context; do not invent reassurance. Accurate facts can still induce inappropriate stopping. Clinical review remains necessary.

required_display_notices.text: Human clinical framing review remains required. This generated answer is not clinically validated.
required_display_notices.origin: Application output contracts; not source-authored medical findings

pagination.notice: Use only a returned continuation. Otherwise this is a bounded response with unknown completeness, not an exhaustive result set. Source-specific page arguments remain documented in tool schemas.

tools.name: get_lactmed_record
tools.description:
Does: Get LactMed text for one record: use during lactation, drug levels, effects on
breastfed infants and on lactation. Alternate Drugs to Consider is excluded from
returned text and synthesis; this tool never recommends a substitution. First call search_lactmed and pass
its numeric id as book_id. Never pass a drug name or invent a record ID.
Separate measured exposure, observed infant outcomes, and source recommendations.
A recommendation to monitor a symptom is NOT evidence that the symptom occurred.
Conversely, a symptom monitored in a study is NOT a recommendation to monitor it.
In every record summary, include a Measured exposure row using exposure_measurements:
give retrieved milk concentration values AND units with source context, plus infant-level
availability. A qualitative low/trace summary alone is incomplete when numerical measurements
were returned. If omitting measurements, explicitly disclose the omission. Read compartment
context; never label maternal-serum measurements as milk or infant serum.
Concentrations are research findings, not administered doses. Omit administered regimens
when doses are excluded, while retaining the requested exposure findings.
Keep each study's exact comparator, co-exposures and specimen terminology separate.
Do not narrow unspecified infant levels to blood or serum.
Preserve separate case-report events and timing: do not merge exposure changes
with outcome observations, infer unstated timing, or imply proven causation.
Include only relevant supported details; explicitly identify unspecified timing.
For partial chronology, group only explicitly linked events rather than a fully
ordered sequence; name the specific ordering that remains unknown.
If outcome text is truncated, retrieve more with max_chars (up to 20000) or
state the limitation; do not infer outcomes from monitoring advice.
Use when: Reading a known lactation-only LactMed record; not pregnancy evidence.
Not for: Searching by drug name; first use search_lactmed.
First/next: Call route_parent_question on the actual question; confirm ambiguous medication identity with normalize_drug before evidence lookup.

dataset.name: mprint-v1
dataset.method: Read-only MCP schema/resource inspection and actual tool calls; implementation and tests not read. Source rows accessed solely through MCP. Answer calculations independently asserted from captured structured responses.
limits: Gold search has no offset; complete narrow cohorts or explicitly bounded 9-record cohorts are used.
Some tasks are moderate difficulty; not all require dozens of calls.
Questions are independent despite shared source cohorts.
Frozen dataset inclusion/classification does not establish efficacy, safety, study quality, funding or complete literature coverage.
Null/absent exported rows are not zero clinical events or absence of original-paper evidence.
Raw traces include historical source observations; retain safety metadata when using evidence outside exact-answer evaluation.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Find all caffeine records using the PK study-type filter, without a population filter. Inspect their PK-summary outcomes to locate the study comparing infants with and without apnoea. For its BPD rows, calculate the apnoeic-group event proportion minus the apnoea-free-group event proportion, using each row's own Subjects n denominator. Return the difference in percentage points as a number with exactly two decimal places, without a percent sign. Do not interpret it as a drug effect.
verification_steps: Inspect candidate outcomes and follow continuations.
Select paired BPD counts and their own denominators.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Among caffeine Gold records carrying both pharmacokinetic and clinical-trial labels, find the study whose PK-summary outcomes are organized by study site. Review every site, excluding the Total category. Which site has a nonzero exported mortality value while both its seizure and heart-rhythm-disturbance values are zero? Return the exact site label only.
questions.derivation: PMID 31101409 has 50 rows; Site 4 death=0.03, Seizures=0, Arrhythmia=0. Sites 1-3 fail at least one condition.
verification_steps: Group by site and exclude Total.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Find the complete set of sertraline Gold records selected by the lactation and PK filters. Cross-check each PMID against the automated Silver classifications. Exactly one candidate has an additional label for biological indicators, beyond the shared pharmacokinetic and pharmacoepidemiology labels. Return that candidate's DOI exactly as stored in Gold, without a URL prefix.
questions.derivation: Of PMIDs 38841362, 30116895, 11483479, only 30116895 has Silver Biomarker; its Gold DOI is 10.1007/s00737-018-0905-3.
verification_steps: Query Silver independently for all 3 PMIDs.
Join the unique Biomarker candidate to its Gold DOI.
questions.limitations: Moderate difficulty: approximately four calls, rather than dozens.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. For every metformin Gold record selected by lactation plus PK, join its PMID to both Silver classifications and the Gold PK-summary table. How many distinct PMIDs have all three automated labels for biological indicators, pharmacoepidemiology, and pharmacokinetics, yet return zero rows from the exported PK-summary table? Count only this snapshot condition; do not infer that the original papers lack outcomes. Return an integer only.
questions.derivation: The 4 candidates are 18662299,15932841,12545145,12436333. Silver Biomarker+PE+PK occurs for 15932841 and 12436333, both with matching_rows=0 in Gold PK summaries.
verification_steps: Perform 4 Silver and 4 Gold summary lookups.
Intersect explicit labels with verified zero exported rows.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Find the complete amoxicillin Gold clinical-trial cohort using the CT filter and no population restriction. Inspect each PMID's PE/CT outcomes. Retain only studies with an outcome row whose actual exposure is amoxicillin-clavulanate and whose statistic is a median with an interquartile range. Sum the Gold study-metadata sample sizes for those retained PMIDs, once per PMID. Return the integer only; do not infer exposure from the list of drugs in study_context.
questions.derivation: 31427252: sample size 197 and PC-QOL median/IQR; 30241722: sample size 179 and time-to-resolution median/IQR. 197+179=376.
verification_steps: Inspect actual exposure/statistic/interval fields for all 4.
Join retained PMIDs back to metadata sample sizes.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Select the sertraline Gold CT record with the greatest numeric PMID, not the most recent date. In that record's PE/CT outcome table, compare each exposure's three correlation-coefficient values relating depression scales to Asberg. For each exposure compute maximum minus minimum. Which exposure has the largest spread? Return the exact Exposure string, and use the outcome rows rather than assuming every row belongs to the drug named in study metadata.
questions.derivation: PMID 39626074 has 9 rows. Estradiol spread=0.70-0.34=0.36; Sertraline=0.65-0.48=0.17; Placebo=0.64-0.45=0.19.
verification_steps: Find greatest numeric PMID under CT filter.
questions.limitations: Moderate difficulty: two or more calls with cross-row arithmetic.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Find all fluoxetine Gold records selected by lactation plus PK, then identify the PMID with the largest number of distinct automated Silver study-type labels. Inspect all of its PK-summary rows, retaining only rows with study_context_matched=true to avoid counting workbook copies. Subtract the maternal reported mean post/pre-exposure percentage for serotonin from the infant whole-blood reported mean post/pre-exposure percentage. Use the stored percentage summaries, not ratios recalculated from mean concentrations. Return the percentage-point difference with exactly one decimal place and no unit.
questions.derivation: 14595087 has 4 labels, uniquely most in the 9-record cohort. Matched workbook rows 5146 and 5149 report 14.5% maternal and 103.6% pediatric; 103.6-14.5=89.1.
verification_steps: Query all 9 Silver records and compare label counts.

questions.question: Use only the bundled MPRINT snapshot revision 4bdee90dff3610816e86d0eed29b4c4d0fe76e89. This is a dataset audit, not a treatment or safety question. Within the complete fluoxetine Gold lactation-plus-PK cohort, find the only PMID that also receives an automated Silver clinical-trial label. Page through its PK-summary outcomes and use only study_context_matched=true rows. Calculate (mean weight at 12 months minus mean birth weight) for the fluoxetine group, then subtract the same change for the control group. Keep the groups separate and ignore duplicate workbook exports. Return the resulting number of grams as an integer only. This arithmetic is not a causal treatment-effect estimate.
questions.derivation: 12709723 is the only CT-labeled candidate. Matched rows 1880-1883: (9760-3380)-(9830-3510)=6380-6320=60 g.
verification_steps: Query Silver labels for each PMID.
Select the 26 context-matched rows rather than 4 workbook copies.
